newsitem.title: UK: Oil price rally stalls as traders take profits.
newsitem.headline: Oil price rally stalls as traders take profits.

text.p: A rally which swept world oil prices to another post-Gulf War high on Tuesday stalled on Wednesday afternoon as traders rushed to cash in profits after sharp morning gains.
But persistent low heating fuel stocks heading into winter and buoyant demand will keep a floor under prices. Some traders expect even sharper gains when the cold weather hits.
At 1550 GMT, December Brent crude oil futures on London's International Petroleum Exchange stood at $23.88 a barrel, 23 cents down on the day and a sharp 52 cents off Wednesday's high.
"The market got a case of the jitters here. People seem to be questioning whether this market should be quite as high as it is," a London broker said.

Traders attributed Wednesday's early strength to bullish reaction to an American Petroleum Institute (API) report that inventories of distillate including heating oil in the U.S. Northeast, the world's largest heating fuel market, fell last week to a shocking 43 percent below 1995 levels.
"The low stock situation in the U.S. Northeast is a cause of concern on the oil market as winter approaches," said Peter Gignoux, head of the London energy desk at Smith, Barney.
Adding to Wednesday's early bullishness was news that supplies of North Sea benchmark Brent would be lower in November by about 2.26 million barrels.
"Any signs of supply shortfalls will rally this market. I would look to buy any dips," said Bo Van Wijk, vice president of energy derivatives at Swiss bank UBS in Zurich.

Brent stands a massive $9 above this time last year and has added $7 in value since mid-June, driven by concern over tensions in the oil-rich Middle East and persistently low stocks of heating oil in key markets in the United States and Europe where stocks are about 10 percent down on last year's already slim levels.
